Phase 5, the three Wikipedia-only people. w13-thin-people.json recorded all three as NOT LANDED and named the dead ends it hit: washingtontimes.com 403 for Milley, cbc.ca 403 for Friedman, and the Navy FOIA reading room rejecting the request for Corbell. Those dead ends are all still dead. This pass landed all three anyway, by going at a different fact rather than a different host.

The move that worked: stop looking for a second copy of the fact the Wikipedia article was carrying, and look for a primary record that attests something the node actually asserts.

STANTON FRIEDMAN. The USAF's own 'The Roswell Report: Fact versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1995) states that 'In 1978, a UFO researcher, Stanton Friedman, met with Marcel and began investigating the claims that the material Marcel handled was from a crashed UFO.' The board carried that as claim 2 sourced to 'Friedman's own account, repeated in his books and in the standard Roswell literature'. It is now attested by the Air Force. The same report lists 'Crash at Corona (1992) by Stanton T. Friedman and Don Berliner' among the works it reviewed. Friedman's own 'Top Secret/MAJIC' (1996), which claim 3 cited by title with no URL, is a full scan on archive.org.

JEREMY CORBELL. Not the USS Omaha confirmation, which is still unreachable. The 26 July 2023 House Oversight hearing record carries, in its Index of Documents, 'Report, Jeremy Corbell, ``The UAP Puzzle''; submitted by Rep. Burchett', and Burchett on the floor: 'I know I saw out in the crowd there George Knapp, my buddy, Jeremy Corbell. They are not witnesses, but they have provided some statements on this subject, and I seek unanimous consent to enter those statements into the record.' That is a congressional primary for the structural role the narrative claims for him.

MARK MILLEY. The 6 August 2023 remark is still unsourceable from here: it was a Washington Times exclusive interview, washingtontimes.com returns 403, and web.archive.org is unreachable from this session entirely. The claim keeps its existing description and stays Tier 2. What is now sourced is the structural fact the narrative rests on -- that he was Chairman of the Joint Chiefs across the period. He testified as Chairman before House Armed Services on 29 March 2023; the transcript lists him as 'Milley, General Mark A., USA, Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff' and carries his prepared statement in the Appendix at page 122.

WILLIAM L. MOORE. Same 1995 USAF report, which reviewed 'The Roswell Incident (1980) by William Moore and Charles Berlitz' and 'Crashed Saucers: Evidence in Search of Proof (1985) by Moore' as part of its records search. His node rested on a scan of the book itself; it now also rests on the Air Force's account of it.

NEGATIVE FINDING, recorded so nobody re-runs it. The 1995 report does NOT name James Ragsdale or Gerald Anderson -- zero occurrences of either across 1.4MB of text. Both are named extensively in the 1997 'Case Closed' (Ragsdale 49 times, including a full interview transcript at page 215; Gerald Anderson 10), which is already their source. That is consistent with both men coming forward after the 1995 report, and it means there is no second USAF document to find for them. They stay at one source, and the single source is a US Air Force report that devotes a transcript to one of them, which is not thin in substance.

ALSO CHECKED AND ABSENT. Of the 32 thin-sourced people, only Corbell, Ryder, Raskin and Higgins appear in the three House UAP hearing transcripts at all. Gradisher, Garrity, Crosson, Langhout, Kerr, McCasland, Rich, Teller, McDonald, Low, Moore, Ragsdale, Anderson, Cameron, Rojas, McMillan, Jiang, Norlain, Lebeau, Platov, Girao and Venturelli appear in none of them. OSTI holds nothing under Friedman's name from his industrial period, and NASA NTRS returned nothing.

TIERING. The Friedman, Corbell, Moore and Milley claims below are written Tier 1 and should stay there: govinfo.gov is a primary-record host and the USAF report is a released government document. The archive.org book scans are written Tier 2, because archive.org is a host of record for a commercially published book rather than a government repository, and PRIMARY_URL_PAT is deliberately narrow.

ROUND 2, after widening PRIMARY_URL_PAT. archive.org/details/DTIC_* is the Defense Technical Information Center archive mirror -- every item carries creator 'Defense Technical Information Center' and sits in the dticarchive and government-documents collections. Adding it to PRIMARY_URL_PAT is the same reasoning the pattern already applies to The Black Vault and irp.fas.org: primacy belongs to the document, not to who serves it. Without it the USAF's own 1995 Roswell report and all three volumes of the Condon Report counted as no primary record at all, and the Friedman claims above were demoted on a node that had just gained an Air Force document.

That unlocked two more. ROBERT LOW: the Condon Report says verbatim 'Assistant Dean Robert J. Low of the Graduate School was appointed project coordinator', and its own index carries 'Low, Robert J., 915-917 / appointed to Colorado project, viii / quoted on Fuller article, 915'. JAMES McDONALD: 'The help of Dr. McDonald, Institute for Atmospheric Physics, University of Arizona, who conducted a study of UFO phenomena concurrently with this study, was invaluable in bringing a number of cases to our attention.'

The 1968 House Symposium on Unidentified Flying Objects, McDonald's other venue, is NOT on govinfo -- the search returns nothing for it or for any Committee on Science and Astronautics UFO print. His nicap.org copy stays as the source for that.

ROUND 3. gerald-anderson and jim-ragsdale already rested on 'Case Closed', but at archive.org/details/AFD-101027-030, which is not a DTIC path and so did not register as a primary record. The identical report exists as DTIC ADA326147, creator 'Defense Technical Information Center', in the dticarchive collection. Adding it gives both nodes a second source and a primary-record URL for the same document they already stood on.

A correction to round 2's negative finding: I first read the DTIC scan as naming Gerald Anderson zero times. It names him 80 times, the same as the other scan. The DTIC OCR double-spaces between words and my two-word grep missed every one. The round 2 finding that the 1995 'Fact versus Fiction' report names neither man still stands -- that was checked with single-word greps.

TRIAGE OF THE REST. Of the 26 people still on one source, NONE rests on an encyclopedic source; that class is now empty. Nine already rest on a primary record (govinfo, lanl.gov, theblackvault, doi.org, Chile's DGAC) and are thin only by count. The remaining seventeen rest on one non-primary source, and that is the number worth working: merge.py now reports it separately as person_single_nonprimary_source so the queue means something. One of the seventeen deserves attention beyond its count: yury-platov's only source is a web.archive.org capture, and web.archive.org is unreachable from this session entirely, so that node currently rests on a source nobody here can open.

ROUND 4, and it reverses an access finding. w13-thin-people.json recorded cbc.ca as returning 403 and gave up on the obituary it wanted for Friedman. cbc.ca answers this environment now. Re-testing every host that earlier passes wrote off is cheap and it changed three answers tonight: cbc.ca and compassrosepllc.com now return 200, today.wayne.edu now returns 200. thehill.com and newsnationnow.com returned 429 rather than 403, which is this session's own crawl rate-limiting itself, not a block. **A host recorded as blocked should be re-tested, not trusted.**

The obituary does NOT carry the industrial-career detail the board's demoted claim needs -- there is no mention of General Electric, Aerojet, Westinghouse, TRW or McDonnell Douglas in it. That claim stays Tier 2 on the encyclopedic source. What CBC does give is the death, the age, the circumstances, and the location of his papers: about 300 boxes at the Provincial Archives of New Brunswick, which is where anyone wanting to settle the industrial-career question will have to go.

CBC News reports that Friedman died suddenly at Toronto Pearson Airport on the Monday night of 13 May 2019, aged 84, while returning from a speaking engagement in Columbus, Ohio, and describes him as 'a nuclear physicist by training' who 'had devoted his life to researching and investigating UFOs since the late 1960s'. The City of Fredericton declared 27 August 2007 Stanton Friedman Day.

Friedman began donating his research collection to the Provincial Archives of New Brunswick in the months before his death. Archivist Joanna Aiton-Kerr told CBC the archives had received about 300 boxes -- roughly 60 metres laid end to end -- and expected several more cargo vans. This is where the primary material behind his Roswell and MJ-12 work now sits, and it is not online.
